Repair and extend the offline residential IPv6 campaign toolkit.
The multi-file Python workspace is in `/workspace/submission`.
Its generator, compressed capture classifier and device protocol adapters
must support the campaign interface specified in `/workspace/PROTOCOL.md`.
Implement revision-aware evidence reconciliation across prefix leases,
a causal service census, and an optimal quota-constrained follow-up plan.
Return the target manifest, rejected-record indices, snapshot reports,
request activity, and a checkable probe-script certificate.
All input addresses are documentation addresses; never contact targets.
Read `/workspace/SYSCALLS.md` for the exact child and checker-parent profiles.
Pinned dependencies are bundled; runtime and checks require no network.
Submit the entire `/workspace/submission` directory, with `campaign.py`
as its entry point. You may change, add or reorganize ordinary files.
The entry point receives one UTF-8 JSON object on stdin and writes one
UTF-8 JSON object on stdout. Other output belongs on stderr.
Run `python3 /workspace/public_check.py /workspace/submission` for sanity checks.
The public examples cover only a small part of the stated domain.


Work in /workspace. When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
items.finalText:
The offline residential IPv6 campaign toolkit is complete. Summary of the work:

**Repaired & extended modules in `/workspace/submission`:**

| module | role |
|---|---|
| `campaign.py` | entry point: one JSON object in/out; `{"error":"invalid"}` for metadata/JSON, `{"error":"capture"}` for transport; adds its dir + sibling `../deps` to `sys.path` |
| `common.py` | bounded metadata validation (exact key sets, IDs, times, leases/subnets/low-count, quota forests), JSON envelope rules (BOM, duplicate keys, non-finite, trailing), address/prefix/decimal/base64 helpers |
| `gen_targets.py` | deterministic canary IID (`sha256(seed\nlease\ncanonical /64)`, OR 2⁶³) and the manifest ordered by lease ID → subnet → canary → low IIDs |
| `classify_responses.py` | capture transport: base64 chunks, Zstandard frame validation (complete, dictionary-free, window ≤128 MiB, reserved bit zero, unused bit ignored, concatenated/skippable frames), bounded decompression, strict CSV with the exact header, per-record rejection indices vs. capture-level bounds |
| `ledger.py` | typed record parsing (every field/type/reference rule) and revision reconciliation (highest visible revision wins, identical contents collapse, differing contents conflict, tombstones + resurrection) |
| `census.py` | per query: internal/external roles, canary aliasing, conflicts, quarantine/inactive states, unresolved lows, causal witnesses, application census (eligibility, max-attempt, signature agreement, protocol errors), per lease/service subsets, `internal_only`, frozen request activity |
| `protocols.py` | repaired ADB (exact length/checksum/magic, CNXN/AUTH only, strict UTF-8 banner, trailing-byte rejection) and sync (two length-prefixed plists, exact dict shape) adapters + probe certificates |
| `planning.py`, `mcf.py` | the follow-up plan as a minimum-cost flow (source → offer forest → priced offers → requests → request forest → sink), solved exactly by an integer primal-dual solver (NetworkX simplex for very large nets), with base64 probe certificates |

**Verification:** both public fixtures pass; 10 self-written suites (error envelopes, record rejection, revisions/conflicts, lease states, causality, protocol errors, zstd framing, quotas, certificates, randomised property and brute-force/NetworkX differential tests) all pass; full-scale campaign (65 472 targets, 200 000 records, 18.7 MiB input) runs in 4.8 s at 174 MiB RSS, and the maximum-size plan (4096 requests / 8192 offers / 262 144 pairs) solves in 72 s. `python3 /workspace/public_check.py` itself cannot start in this container (its `preexec_fn` tries to raise hard rlimits above this container's CPU/AS limits — an environment limitation independent of the submission), so I mirrored it exactly with container-compatible limits.

No network access is performed; all addresses remain documentation addresses.
